title: Anime Dice Codes: Working Codes & How to Redeem
description: Working Anime Dice codes checked September 28, 2026, with the left-side Shop redeem path and what to try when a pasted code is rejected.
searchIntent: Find working Anime Dice codes and redeem them in the Shop.

hero.heading: Anime Dice Codes
hero.lead: Checked September 28, 2026. Redeem these in the left-side Shop, at the Enter Code box.

sections.intro: These 16 codes were still active on September 28, 2026. UPDATE2, UPDATE1 and RELEASE show exact rewards. Every other row is a reward bundle.

sections.heading: How to Redeem Anime Dice Codes
sections.intro: The code box is inside Shop, not in a settings menu. Use the Shop button on the left side of the screen.

steps.heading: Open Anime Dice
steps.description: Launch the Roblox experience and wait until you can move around your plot.

steps.heading: Click Shop on the left
steps.description: Press the Shop button on the left side of the screen. This is the same column as Rebirth and Index.

steps.heading: Scroll to the bottom
steps.description: Move to the bottom of the Shop window until the code field is visible.

steps.heading: Enter the code
steps.description: Type or paste one code into the Enter Code box. Match the capital letters, with no extra spaces.

steps.heading: Press the green Redeem
steps.description: Click the green Redeem button. A working code adds the reward immediately.

paragraphs: Redeem one code at a time. If the button does nothing, clear the box and paste the code again before you try the next one.

Lucky Spins, Trait Rerolls and Gems are the rewards players are cashing these codes in for. A row marked Reward bundle is a working code. Redeem it the same way. The bundle is the freebie pack for that code, including the likes codes, the CCU codes, and UPDATE3 through UPDATE6.

sections.heading: Expired Anime Dice Codes
paragraphs: The September 28, 2026 lists still treat the 16 codes in the table as active. JPCALLING sits in the limited section above, not in this expired list.
If a code in the table fails after a clean paste on a fresh server, skip it and redeem the next one. A code this account has already claimed will fail too, even when it still works for someone else.

sections.heading: Why a Code May Not Work
paragraphs: Most failed redemptions are a typing problem. Anime Dice codes are case sensitive. UPDATE6 is not the same string as update6, and a space copied from a chat message is enough to make Redeem refuse it.

A code can also be used up. JPCALLING was already described as limited-use, so try the 16 working codes first. Milestone codes such as 400KLIKES can stay active for a long time, then stop without a separate announcement.

If the string is exact and the code is still in the table, leave the experience and join again. A new code sometimes reaches one server before another. Redeeming on a fresh server is the check to make before you decide the code is dead.

Already redeemed codes do not pay twice on the same account. A second try of RELEASE, UPDATE1 or UPDATE2 will fail if that account has already claimed it, even though the code still works for someone else.

sections.heading: Where New Anime Dice Codes Appear
paragraphs: New Anime Dice codes have been arriving with updates and with like or player-count milestones. UPDATE6 is the update code in the current set. 400KLIKES, 250KLIKES, 100KLIKES and the CCU codes follow the milestone pattern.

The developer is More & More Games. Their Roblox group and Discord are the places new strings are posted. The official Roblox game page is the place to confirm you are in the current version of Anime Dice before you troubleshoot a code.
This page is the working list after those posts have been compared. A code that shows up in only one roundup stays off the table until a second current list agrees.

faq.question: How do you redeem codes in Anime Dice?
faq.answer: Open Anime Dice, click Shop on the left, scroll to the bottom of the Shop window, type the code into Enter Code, and press the green Redeem button.

faq.question: What do UPDATE2, UPDATE1 and RELEASE give?
faq.answer: UPDATE2 gives 2 Lucky Spins, 5 Trait Rerolls and 5 Gems. UPDATE1 gives 2 Lucky Spins, 3 Trait Rerolls and 3 Gems. RELEASE gives 1 Lucky Spin, 2 Trait Rerolls and 2 Gems. The other working codes are a reward bundle. Claim them with the same Redeem button for the freebie pack.

faq.question: Why was a code rejected?
faq.answer: Check the capital letters, remove spaces, and confirm you have not already redeemed that code on this account. If it is a brand-new code, rejoin so you land on an updated server, then paste it again.

sections.heading: Best Anime Dice Units
paragraphs: Enol is the unit to keep when it appears. The matching Index listings put its base income at $9.1K/s, with base odds of 1 in 290K. That is several times the next recorded earner. A plain Enol already out-earns a plain Sakuna, and a Grade or Trait on Enol widens the gap further.

Sakuna at $2K/s, Madera at $1.5K/s and Maheto at $1.1K/s are the rest of S. They are the copies that should occupy plot pads before you worry about perfecting a B or C unit. Todoh, Super Saiyen and Goko are the A band: strong enough to keep, and the right pads to fill while you are still rolling for S.

Zaro leads B at $219/s. Hasoka, Deko, Bakuga and Todoraki follow. They are the units that carry a fresh plot after Rebirth, because your placed units stay and these base incomes are high enough to rebuild cash. They are not where Trait Rerolls should go if an A or S copy is already in the backpack.

Everything from Tanjuro down to Naroto is early cash. Naroto is 1 in 2 at $1/s. It will show up constantly. A plain Naroto is not a project. The exception is a mutated or oversized copy: compare that copy's own Income per second with the unit already on the pad before you sell it.

sections.heading: How This Ranking Is Set
paragraphs: Tier placement uses the recorded base income and the base Index odds that match across current public Index listings. It is not a claim that every copy of a name performs the same. Grade, Trait, size and Mutation are copy-level modifiers, and they can make a lower name earn more than a plain higher name.

Damage and Health are not in this table. Those stats matter in Tower, and the Index listings used here record income and odds, not a full combat sheet. If two copies have similar income, the one you can actually clear floors with is the one to keep for Tower, even if this income ranking likes the other name.

Base Index odds are the listed 1-in figure for the plain character. Dice Luck, Rebirth Luck and potions change your real chance. A 1 in 290K Enol is not a promise about your next roll. It is the comparison number printed for that Index entry.

Read a new pull in this order. First, look at the Income per second on that copy. Second, look for a mutation name or a Huge or Titanic size. Third, look at Grade and Trait. The name's tier tells you whether the plain version is a keeper. The copy's modifiers tell you whether this particular one is.

faq.answer: On recorded base income, S is Enol ($9.1K/s), Sakuna ($2K/s), Madera ($1.5K/s) and Maheto ($1.1K/s). Enol is far ahead of the other three.

faq.question: What is the best Anime Dice unit?
faq.answer: Enol has the highest recorded base income, at $9.1K/s and 1 in 290K. A modified copy of another unit can still earn more than a plain Enol, so compare the Income per second on the copies you actually own.

faq.question: Should I upgrade Naroto?
faq.answer: A plain Naroto is the most common unit and the lowest recorded earner, at $1/s. Do not spend Gems or Trait Rerolls on it. Check a mutated or oversized Naroto against the unit already on your pad before you sell that copy.

faq.question: Do grades change the tier list?
faq.answer: Yes. This order is base income for a plain copy. A high Grade, an all-stat Trait, or a mutation can move a lower name above a plain unit from a higher tier.

hero.heading: Anime Dice Traits
hero.lead: Thirteen traits. Four of them multiply Income, Damage and Health together. A new roll replaces the trait on that unit.

sections.heading: Anime Dice Trait List
sections.intro: These effects and chances match the Traits panel figures repeated by several September 2026 guides, including menu screenshots. A dash means that trait does not list a multiplier for that stat.

sections.heading: Best Anime Dice Traits
paragraphs: Transcendent is the best trait in the list: 15x Income, 15x Damage and 15x Health, at 0.006%. Monarch is the next all-stat result at 8x and 0.025%. Shogun is 5x at 0.12%, and Samurai is 3x at 0.5%. If any of those four lands on a unit you still place, stop rerolling that unit.

Money III, Damage III and Health III are the best single-stat results, each at 2x and 1.2%. Money belongs on a unit that sits on a plot pad and makes cash. Damage and Health belong on units you bring to Tower. A 2x Money trait does nothing for a floor clear, and a 2x Damage trait is the wrong target if the unit's only job is income.

Tier II traits are 1.5x at 6.3%, and tier I traits are 1.2x at 25.4%. Most rolls land in that common range. That is why spending Trait Rerolls on Naroto, Ichiga or any other unit you are about to replace is the usual waste. Hold the rerolls until the unit is one you would still equip after your next dice upgrade.

Samurai is the realistic all-stat stop for most accounts. Half a percent is still rare, but it is much closer than Transcendent. Tripling all three stats already beats any 2x single-stat trait on raw value. Keep Samurai unless you have a large reroll stack and the unit is one of the S-tier income names.

sections.heading: How Trait Rerolls Work
paragraphs: A unit holds one trait. The new result replaces the old one. There is no way to store the previous trait on that same copy, so do not reroll Transcendent, Monarch, Shogun or a Samurai you are happy with.

Open the Traits station in the hub, select the unit, and roll. Each roll spends 1 Trait Reroll. Codes such as UPDATE2, UPDATE1 and RELEASE are a direct source of those rerolls, and Tower rewards and the Shop are the other sources players use.

The trait and the Grade are separate. Rolling a trait does not change the Grade, and rolling a Grade does not change the trait. A keeper wants both: a high Income Grade for cash, and either Money or an all-stat trait depending on whether that copy is a pad unit or a Tower unit.

faq.question: What is the best trait in Anime Dice?
faq.answer: Transcendent, at 15x Income, 15x Damage and 15x Health. Monarch is 8x across the same three stats, Shogun is 5x, and Samurai is 3x.

faq.question: How do you reroll a trait?
faq.answer: Go to the Traits station, select the unit, and roll. Each attempt spends 1 Trait Reroll and replaces the trait already on that unit.

faq.question: Should I reroll Money I?
faq.answer: Reroll it on a unit you are keeping. Leave it on a filler you expect to sell or replace. Money I is a 1.2x Income result at 25.4%, so it is a common roll, not a stop.

faq.question: Do traits affect damage and cash?
faq.answer: The four named traits multiply Income, Damage and Health. Money traits multiply Income only. Damage traits multiply Damage only. Health traits multiply Health only.

paragraphs: Gujo, Levy, Pikolo and Zenitsa appear as Index names alongside the 24 units above. Read odds and income on the card for the copy you rolled, then compare that Income per second with the unit on your worst pad.
If the current Index shows a name that is not in this table, use that same card check. A newer update can add a character before a base-income row is worth copying into a ranking.

If you roll one of the four, use the Income per second on that copy and the tier list rule for modified units: a mutation, a Huge or Titanic size, a high Grade, or an all-stat trait can make it a keeper even without a published base row.
The names in this game are the in-game spellings. Naroto, Goko, Friza, Enol and the rest are the labels on the Index. They are not renamed here to match an anime series.

sections.heading: How to Read a Pull
paragraphs: Open the unit card before you sell anything. The card is where Income, the trait and the grade show up together. The Index is where you check the base 1-in value for the plain name. The Backpack is the list of copies you actually own, including mutated ones.

A 1-in number is not your personal drop rate. Better dice and a higher Luck multiplier from Rebirth improve rolls, and the Index figure stays the label for that character. Enol can say 1 in 290K on the Index while your Luck makes the practical wait shorter or longer than another player's.

Sort keepers by the income on the copy, then by the name's base tier. An S name with a bad grade can lose to an A name with Z or an all-stat trait. Look at the number on the card after modifiers, then decide which pad it replaces.

Sell plain duplicates of D and C units once every pad has something better. Do that at the Sell Units stand after you have checked the duplicate for a mutation or a size tag. A Silver, Gold, Emerald, Diamond, Ruby or Rainbow label is a reason to pause.

sections.heading: How Grades Work in Anime Dice
paragraphs: A grade is an Income multiplier on one copy. Z+ is 25x Income. Z is 15x, S+ is 10x, S is 7x, A+ is 4.5x, A is 3x, B is 1.6x, C is 1.2x and D is 1.1x. The gap from D to Z+ is the whole point of the system: the same unit name can be a minor earner or the best pad on the plot.
Grades do not add Damage or Health. Tower performance comes from the unit, its trait, and your Damage and Health upgrades. Use Gems on the copy whose job is cash.

Open the Grades station, select the unit, and roll with the Gem button. The new letter replaces the old one. Spend that roll on a unit you will still place after the next dice upgrade. A D or C on Enol is worth chasing. A Z+ on a plain Naroto is a strong multiplier on a $1/s base, and it can still lose to a plain Sakuna or Maheto. Read the copy's Income per second after the roll, not the letter alone.

Gems also come from codes. UPDATE2 includes 5 Gems, UPDATE1 includes 3, and RELEASE includes 2. Redeem the other working codes before you sit down at the Grades station. Their reward is a bundle of freebies, and the Shop button is the same one used for UPDATE2.

sections.heading: Which Grade to Stop On
paragraphs: Stop on Z+ . It is the highest multiplier in the agreed list. Z at 15x is also a stop for almost every unit. S+ and S are stops on a long-term earner if your Gem stack is small. A+ and A are fine while you are still filling pads, and they are worth replacing later on an S-tier name.
D, C and B are not targets. They are what most rolls will show. Leave a low grade on a unit you are about to replace, and keep rolling only on the names in the tier list's S and A bands.

Roll one grade, then look at the pad. If the new Income per second beats the unit you would take off, place the copy and stop. If it does not, leave the low letter on a filler and spend the next Gems on Enol, Sakuna, Madera or Maheto.

After a grade roll, look at Income per second on the card rather than treating the letter as a trophy. A Z on a low base-income starter can still lose a pad to a plain Sakuna, Madera or Maheto. The letter tells you the multiplier. The card tells you the result.

faq.question: What are the Anime Dice grades?
faq.answer: D, C, B, A, A+, S, S+, Z and Z+. Their Income multipliers are 1.1x, 1.2x, 1.6x, 3x, 4.5x, 7x, 10x, 15x and 25x.

faq.question: What is the best grade in Anime Dice?
faq.answer: Z+ is the best grade in the agreed list, at 25x Income. Z is next at 15x Income.

faq.question: How do you reroll a grade?
faq.answer: Use the Grades station, select the unit, and roll with the Gem button. The new grade replaces the old one and changes that copy's Income multiplier.

faq.question: Does a grade increase damage?
faq.answer: No. The listed grade effect is Income. Damage and Health come from the unit and from traits, not from the grade letter.

title: Anime Dice Rebirth Guide: Reset, Keep, Cost
description: Anime Dice rebirth resets Cash, raises the Luck and Cash multipliers, and keeps your units. See the early cash requirements and when to press it.
searchIntent: Learn what Anime Dice rebirth resets, what it keeps, and when to press it.

hero.heading: Anime Dice Rebirth
hero.lead: Rebirth clears Cash and raises the Luck and Cash multipliers shown on the panel. Units, dice and upgrades stay.

sections.heading: What Rebirth Does in Anime Dice
paragraphs: Rebirth is a cash reset with a permanent multiplier. When you confirm it, Cash goes to zero. The Rebirth panel shows the current Luck multiplier and the next one, and the same for the Cash multiplier. Those new multipliers apply on their own. The Luck and Cash upgrade tree is a separate cash purchase, and those upgrades stay after the reset.

The button sits on the left side of the screen, between Shop and Index. Open it before you confirm, and read both the cash requirement and the two before-and-after multiplier rows. If the requirement on your panel does not match a number you saw in a guide, use the panel.

table.caption: What an Anime Dice rebirth changes
rows: Resets to zero. Cash above the requirement is deleted too.
Moves to the next value printed on the Rebirth panel.
Moves to the next value printed on the Rebirth panel.
Stay. They are not sold back or cleared.
Grade and Trait on a unit

sections.heading: Rebirth Cash Requirements
sections.intro: The first two rebirths. From the third onward, the cash requirement and the next multipliers are the numbers on your Rebirth panel.
paragraphs: The first rebirth is the $50,000 cash reset that moves both multipliers from 1x to 1.5x. The second is the $5,000,000 reset that moves them from 1.5x to 2x. From the third rebirth onward, the panel prints the next cash requirement and the next multiplier pair. Use that screen each time. It stays current when a later update changes a checkpoint.

Current versions keep going well past those two steps. Older gameplay already reaches later multiplier stages, and the cash required at those stages is large enough that a starter plot cannot pay it. Later thresholds can move when the game updates. The in-game Rebirth panel is the number to use, including when it shows a final multiplier step.

A higher multiplier is account progress. The Cash multiplier makes the units already on your plot earn more. The Luck multiplier improves later rolls. Neither one restores the cash you just deleted, so the plot has to earn the next requirement itself.

sections.heading: When to Rebirth in Anime Dice

steps.heading: Read the panel
steps.description: Open Rebirth and check the cash requirement plus the next Luck and Cash multipliers. That screen is the cost that matters.

steps.heading: Spend cash above the cost
steps.description: Buy the next dice or the next Money and Luck upgrades you can afford. Leftover cash is wiped, so do not sit on a large surplus.

steps.heading: Leave keepers on pads
steps.description: Units stay. A full plot of your best income copies is what rebuilds cash after the number hits zero.

steps.heading: Confirm, then refill
steps.description: Press Rebirth. Cash reads zero and the multipliers update. Put a unit on every pad you have so income starts again immediately.

paragraphs: Press Rebirth when the panel requirement is affordable and the units on your plot can earn that kind of cash again without a long stall. The first $50,000 reset is worth taking once you can spend down to it and still have units placed. Waiting with a huge unused balance does not help, because the unused part is deleted.

Do not rebirth if the only units you have are plain starters and the next requirement is one of the large later figures. The multipliers help, but they multiply the income of the units you kept. A plot of Naroto and Ichiga rebuilds a $50,000 reset. It does not comfortably rebuild a hundreds-of-millions reset.

Extra plot slots are also reported as you rebirth, which is another reason the kept units matter. More pads only help after you have units worth placing on them. Use the character list and the tier list to decide who goes back down first.

faq.question: What does rebirth do in Anime Dice?
faq.answer: It sets Cash to zero and raises the Luck multiplier and the Cash multiplier to the next values on the Rebirth panel. Units, dice, upgrades, Gems and Trait Rerolls stay.

faq.question: How much is the first Anime Dice rebirth?
faq.answer: The first rebirth costs $50,000 cash and moves Luck and Cash from 1x to 1.5x. The second costs $5,000,000 and moves both from 1.5x to 2x. Use the panel for every rebirth after that.

faq.question: Do units stay after rebirth?
faq.answer: Yes. Units stay on the plot, and the Grade and Trait on each copy stay with it. Cash is the balance that is cleared.

faq.question: When should I rebirth?
faq.answer: When you can pay the panel's cash requirement, you have spent the surplus on dice or upgrades, and the units you are keeping can earn that cash again. Do not hold a large extra balance, because it is deleted.

title: Anime Dice Mutations: Variants You Can Roll
description: Anime Dice mutations are variant labels on a rolled copy, from Silver through Rainbow. See how they differ from traits, grades and size.
searchIntent: See the Anime Dice mutation labels and how a mutated copy drops.

hero.heading: Anime Dice Mutations
hero.lead: A mutation comes on the copy you roll. It is not a station where you pay to mutate a unit you already own.

sections.heading: What Are Anime Dice Mutations?
paragraphs: A mutation is a variant label on a character copy. Silver, Gold, Emerald, Diamond, Ruby and Rainbow are the six labels. The dice reveal the copy with that label already on it. Shop, the Traits station and the Grades station change other parts of a unit. The mutation is the one that came with the roll.

The label is on the copy. A Silver Naroto is not the same object as a plain Naroto, even though the character name matches. Sell checks have to happen before you junk duplicates, because the valuable part may be the variant rather than the name.

The unit card shows the mutation name next to the character. Read the Income per second on that card before you sell the copy. A Rainbow label on a weak base can still lose a pad to a plain Enol, Sakuna or Maheto.

paragraphs: Huge and Titanic are size labels, not mutations. A copy can be both, such as a Huge unit that is also Silver. Size and mutation are reasons to open the card. They are not a second trait slot.

Trait Rerolls do not change the mutation, and the Grades station does not change it either. Those systems edit the trait and the grade on whatever copy you select. The mutation stays the one you rolled.

sections.heading: How to Get Mutations
paragraphs: Roll. Mutations show up on the unit the dice reveal. Better dice and a higher Luck multiplier increase the quality of rolls in general. They are not a separate mutation button.

Lucky Spins, including the ones from UPDATE2, UPDATE1 and RELEASE, are extra rolls. Use them when your dice and Luck upgrades are already in a decent place, so the spin is not spent on the starter setup.

Auto sell can remove a variant if the rule is aimed only at the character name or a low odds band. Before you turn a strict auto-sell rule on, look at a few duplicates by hand and see whether Silver or larger tags are being sold with the plain copies.

sections.heading: Mutation, Grade and Trait
paragraphs: Three different things can sit on one copy. The mutation is the variant you rolled. The grade is the Income letter from the Grades station. The trait is the stat roll from the Traits station. A strong copy can have all three, and a weak name can be worth keeping because of one of them.

Compare Income per second on the card after those modifiers, not the base tier alone. The tier list ranks plain base income. A mutated starter can beat a plain unit from a higher tier. It can also be a flashy label on a copy that still earns less than the Enol or Sakuna already on the pad. The card's income number settles it.
If you decide the mutated copy is a keeper, that is the copy that gets Gems and Trait Rerolls. Do not roll those resources onto a plain duplicate of the same name just because the name matches.

sections.heading: Should You Keep a Mutated Unit?
paragraphs: Keep it when its Income per second is higher than the unit currently on the worst pad, or when you cannot yet tell and the label is one of the six above. Selling is reasonable when the copy earns less than a plain unit you already have placed and you have already read the card.

A mutation is not automatically a Tower carry and not automatically an endgame earner. Damage and Health still depend on the unit and its trait. Income still depends on the base, the grade and the cash multiplier from Rebirth.
Keep one strong copy, not every duplicate of the same label. Extra plain copies of common names can go to the Sell Units stand once the pads are full and the mutated copy is the one you equipped.

faq.question: What are the mutations in Anime Dice?
faq.answer: The mutation labels agreed by current guides are Silver, Gold, Emerald, Diamond, Ruby and Rainbow. Huge and Titanic are sizes, not mutations.

faq.question: How do you get a mutation?
faq.answer: Roll the dice. The mutation is already on the copy when it appears. Lucky Spins are extra rolls of the same kind.

faq.question: Do mutations have a multiplier?
faq.answer: Read the Income on that copy. The card shows the mutation name, and that income number is what you compare with the unit already on the pad.

faq.question: Does a trait reroll change the mutation?
faq.answer: No. A Trait Reroll replaces the trait. A grade roll replaces the grade. The mutation stays on the copy you rolled.

title: How to Play Anime Dice: Beginner Guide
description: How to play Anime Dice: roll a unit, place it, earn Cash, buy dice, redeem codes in Shop, then use Traits, Grades, Index and Rebirth.
searchIntent: Follow the Anime Dice buttons from the first roll through codes, traits, grades and rebirth.

hero.heading: How to Play Anime Dice
hero.lead: Roll a unit, place it on a pad, spend the Cash it makes, and use Shop, Index and Rebirth on the left side of the screen.

steps.heading: Join Anime Dice
steps.description: Open the official Roblox page for Anime Dice, by More & More Games, and join the experience.

steps.heading: Roll
steps.description: Roll the dice you have. The roll reveals a character copy, which may include a mutation or a size label.

steps.heading: Place the unit
steps.description: Put the copy on a plot pad. A unit that stays in the backpack does not earn.

steps.heading: Collect Cash
steps.description: Placed units generate Cash, including while you are offline. Collect it and spend it before a rebirth, because rebirth deletes the cash balance.

steps.heading: Buy better dice
steps.description: Spend Cash in the dice shop on the next die you can afford. Dice are the Luck ladder for later rolls.

steps.heading: Redeem codes in Shop
steps.description: Click Shop on the left, scroll to Enter Code, and redeem the working codes. Rewards include Lucky Spins, Trait Rerolls and Gems.

steps.heading: Use Traits and Grades
steps.description: Trait Rerolls are spent at the Traits station, one per roll. Gems are spent at the Grades station. Use both on units you will keep.

steps.heading: Check the Index
steps.description: Index, on the left, shows the collection and the base 1-in value. Your Backpack shows the copies you own.

steps.heading: Rebirth from the panel
steps.description: Open Rebirth, between Shop and Index. Confirm when the cash requirement is met and your pads can earn it again.

sections.heading: The Left-Side Buttons
paragraphs: Three buttons on the left come up immediately. Shop is where codes are redeemed, at the bottom of that window, and where you buy extra rolls or resources. Rebirth is the cash reset that raises Luck and Cash multipliers. Index is the collection list, not the backpack of copies you are holding.

The hub also has stations rather than more left-side icons. The Traits station takes Trait Rerolls. The Grades station takes Gems and rolls an Income letter from D to Z+. The Sell Units stand is where plain duplicates go after you have read the card. The dice shop is where Cash turns into a higher Luck die.

Tower is the combat side of the same units. Traits that say Damage or Health matter there. Grades do not add those stats. You can ignore Tower for the first stretch of a new account and still progress, because cash from the plot is what buys the next die.

sections.heading: What to Spend First
paragraphs: Cash goes to the next die and to Money and Luck upgrades before it goes to a starter unit you will replace. A better die improves rolls from that point on. A level on plain Naroto does not. Look at the tier list if you are unsure whether the name in your hand is a starter.

Trait Rerolls go to a unit you would still place after the next rebirth. Stop when you hit Samurai, Shogun, Monarch or Transcendent. Money III is a fine stop on a plot earner. Damage III and Health III are the stops for a Tower unit.

Gems go to the same kind of keeper. The grade list runs from D at 1.1x Income to Z+ at 25x Income. Rolling a grade onto a unit you are about to sell spends a Gem you could have used on Enol, Sakuna, Madera, Maheto or the best A unit you have.

Lucky Spins are rolls. They are more useful after the die and the Luck upgrades are no longer the starter setup. Spending them in the first minute is allowed, and it is weaker than spending them once the Luck multiplier from the first rebirth is already on the account.

sections.heading: The First Rebirth Checkpoint
paragraphs: The first rebirth costs $50,000 and moves Luck and Cash from 1x to 1.5x. Spend cash above $50,000 on a die or on upgrades, leave your best units on the pads, then confirm. The second rebirth is $5,000,000, from 1.5x to 2x. Anything beyond that is the number on your own Rebirth panel.

You do not bank cash through the reset, and you do not lose the units. That is the whole timing rule. If the plot can make the requirement again with the units that stay, the new multipliers are worth more than the cash pile. If it cannot, fill the pads with better base-income units first.

faq.question: How do you play Anime Dice?
faq.answer: Roll a character, place it on a plot pad, and spend the Cash it generates on better dice and Luck. Redeem codes in the left Shop, roll traits and grades on keepers, and rebirth when the panel requirement is one your plot can earn again.

faq.question: Where are codes in Anime Dice?
faq.answer: Click Shop on the left side of the screen, scroll to the bottom, enter the code, and press the green Redeem button.

faq.question: What should a new player buy first?
faq.answer: The next die you can afford, plus Money and Luck upgrades. Save Trait Rerolls and Gems for a unit you will still use after that upgrade, not for the first common you roll.

faq.question: What stays when you rebirth?
faq.answer: Units, dice, upgrades, Gems and Trait Rerolls stay. Cash is reset to zero, and the Luck and Cash multipliers increase.
